newsitem.title: CHINA: China stamp smugglers post huge profits from HK.
newsitem.headline: China stamp smugglers post huge profits from HK.

text.p: Freewheeling philatelists from China are smuggling vast numbers of stamps from Hong Kong to sell for huge profits on the mainland as the handover of the British colony nears, the Economic Daily said on Friday.

Chinese customs officials on the border with Hong Kong had so far this year uncovered more than one million stamps worth several million Hong Kong dollars being smuggled out of the territory, the newspaper said.

In stamp black markets, prices for Hong Kong stamps could soar to dozens of times the face value, making them perfect for smugglers looking to turn a quick profit, it said. China levies a 20 percent import duty and 17 percent value-added tax on stamp imports.
"Buying Hong Kong-issued stamps before the handover carries a certain historical significance," it said. "Moreover, stamps are small, easy to carry, have a high profit margin and sell well."

Stamp collecting is a widespread passion in China, and collectors are snapping up anything connected to Hong Kong or the handover, which Beijing has billed as one of the events of year, if not the century.
